o1.biggest_strength: A complete, buildable flow. It matches an offer to each reason, splits groups by plan type and reminder status, gives the exact copy, and adds an optional 'email me in 3/6 months' for trip-over learners, which fits Greg well.
o1.biggest_mistake: It keeps 50% off for 3 months for people switching apps, which goes against my own data on discounts. The value of that group is also loosely counted: 67 people at near full price while they are on half price.
o1.what_would_make_it_a_10: Drop the switcher discount. Put the headline numbers and the warning that the pause carries the result at the top. Give an honest range instead of single figures.

o2.biggest_strength: Leads with the decision and the money, including a range, and flags the risk clearly. The pause does 80% of the work, and without it the flow keeps fewer people than today, so the pause is the critical path for the sprint. It also has a clear measurement plan and a smart bolder idea to prompt reminders before anyone cancels.
o2.biggest_mistake: Trip-over learners get only a plain exit, with no 'remind me before your next trip' option. A little of the copy, such as 'It helps us help you', sounds more corporate than warm.
o2.what_would_make_it_a_10: Add the optional remind-me email for trip-over learners. Warm up the screen 1 subtitle. Show the full working for the 12-month revenue figure.

reason: Both are flows my team could build. The second one tells me what matters most up front: bring back the pause first or the whole thing fails. It drops the discount completely and tells me how to know it's working.
